findings.claim: The rename was not propagated into the batch's own adjudication record: ADJUDICATION.md still reprints the full pre-rename passage, including the real place name Sandviken carrying the invented 1927 cast-iron pissoir fact, plus Norrkoping, Sinikka Vaara and the old q1 stem.
findings.evidence: pipeline/synthetic/batches/batch12/ADJUDICATION.md lines 258, 260, 264, 271 still read 'Sinikka Vaara vid Institutet for stadsnara tjanster i Norrkoping', 'Vaara medger ocksa', 'Men i Sandviken star fortfarande en gjutjarnspissoar fran 1927' and 'Vad kom fram i Sinikka Vaaras undersokning?'. Both earlier batch-12 repairs DID propagate into this same file: grep 'Ferrymouth' = 1 hit and 'Harbor Fog' = 0 hits (elf-b12-003), grep 'Tovedal' = 3 hits (las-b12-001).
findings.why: The batch set its own standard for these repairs ('all mentions propagated', STATUS.md). By that standard the propagation is incomplete: the reviewable record of this unit still displays the exact collision the repair was opened to remove. Shipping content (candidates-final) is clean, so this is a record defect, not a student-facing one. Upstream stage snapshots (candidates/, candidates-corrected/, gen-las-short-1.*) are NOT part of this finding - 'Harbor Fog' survives in those for elf-b12-003 too, so leaving them frozen is the established convention.

findings.claim: The entityfix regate did not reach verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl, so in that file the LAST records for las-b12-002 are still the pre-rename G-KEY lines.
findings.evidence: grep -c entityfix over verdicts-vfinal/: gkey-1 = 2, gkey-2 = 2, gdistractor = 2, gstem = 2, gkey-resolved = 0. In verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl the unit's records are lines 17-18 (vote 1) and 46-47 (vote 2), all plain 'claude-opus-4-8/G-KEY'. Precedent inside the same file shows resolved IS refreshed after a regate: it carries 8 regate3/clean-rerun-derived lines and appends las-b12-001's round-3 votes at lines 55-58.
findings.why: The resolved file is the merged authority for G-KEY; leaving it at the pre-rename state means a reader reconstructing the shipped evidence chain from it alone sees votes cast against a passage that no longer exists. The solve outcome is unaffected - both entityfix votes independently return C/A, matching the keys - so this is a completeness gap, not a correctness one.

findings.claim: A rationale quotation still does not appear verbatim in the passage; it survived a repair round that rewrote the same file.
findings.evidence: q1 rationale: 'barnfamiljer namns faktiskt, men just som den grupp dar sambandet ”knappt gick att belagga alls”'. Passage: 'For barnfamiljer gick det knappt att belagga alls'. Programmatic check of all 8 quoted spans in the current unit: 7 resolve in the passage, this one does not. The prior audit of this unit raised the identical finding; the 2026-07-30 repair touched passage, stem and generator_meta but left the quote unfixed.
findings.why: Integrated-review row 4 (every phrase a rationale quotes must appear in the current text) is the highest-yield post-correction check; a student who searches the passage for the quoted string will not find it. Unchanged severity from the earlier audit - the key is unaffected.

findings.claim: The fresh entityfix G-STEM regate re-raised a major flag on q2 and no disposition was recorded for the 2026-07-30 round.
findings.evidence: verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gstem.jsonl line 6: verdict 'flag', severity major, blind_classification PARTIALLY, blind_pick 'A' - which is the key. reviews/pedagogy.jsonl's new line mentions only the renames and 'keys unchanged'; reviews/integrated.jsonl had no post-rename line until this audit appended one.
findings.why: las-b12-001 was refuted earlier in this campaign precisely for undispositioned G-STEM flags, so the pattern deserves naming. It is only a note here because the finding is a verbatim repeat of one already adjudicated at batch level - ADJUDICATION.md line 252 records the same 'PARTIALLY (blind pick A)' reasoning under 'Grind: SURVIVED_FLAGGED' - so the rename introduced no new blind-answerability risk, only an unlabelled duplicate record.

findings.claim: The originality_note's parenthetical 'bylinen Ola Rimfeldt (ingen barare)' is reproducible only as a statement about the full name; the surname Rimfeldt has real bearers.
findings.evidence: People search returns Karl Erik Rimfeldt, CEO of Rimfeldt Eiendom AS (Kongsvinger, Norway); sv.wikipedia surfaces Kaili Rimfeld (behavioural geneticist, spelt without the final t). No 'Ola Rimfeldt' exists in any index I queried.
findings.why: The claim as written is about the byline, and at that level it verifies - so this is not a false originality_note claim of the Kerrig kind. But 'ingen barare' reads as a claim about the name as such, which is not true of the surname; a future sweep re-reading this note should not treat it as evidence that the surname is invented. Domain is also unrelated (Norwegian real estate vs a Swedish planeringsarkitekt byline), so no collision follows.

findings.claim: The pre-rename names survive inside generator_meta.originality_note, by design.
findings.evidence: Programmatic scan: 'Sandviken', 'Norrkoping', 'Sinikka', 'Vaara' appear only in generator_meta.originality_note, nowhere in passage, stems, options or rationales.
findings.why: Recorded so a future literal grep does not mistake provenance for a leak. This mirrors the elf-b12-003 precedent, where the rewritten originality_note also names the real Benjamin Moore colour it replaced. generator_meta is not student-visible.

findings.claim: The carried-over G-SPRAK vote-1 major on 'Institutet for stadsnara tjanster' remains undispositioned, and the new originality_note re-asserts the name as checked-and-kept.
findings.evidence: verdicts.jsonl G-SPRAK vote 1 major: "'stadsnara' collocates with natur/skog/odling/mark ... as an institute name it reads like a mistranslation of 'urban services'"; the string is unchanged in candidates-final and the originality_note now adds 'Institutet for stadsnara tjanster (inget institut med det namnet finns)'.
findings.why: The originality_note's claim is about existence, which I verified as correct - it is a genuinely fictional institute. It does not address the separate collocation objection, which predates this repair and is carried here only so the two checks are not conflated by a later reader.
